The use of panic in the NewKeeper function for handling invalid authority addresses can lead to an application crash. This is particularly dangerous in a production environment, where an unexpected crash can disrupt service, lead to loss of data, and affect user trust. Using panic for error handling is considered a bad practice as it does not allow for graceful error recovery.

Create an invalid authority address.
Call the NewKeeper function with the invalid address.
Observe that the application panics and crashes.

invalidAddress := sdk.AccAddress("invalid_address")
_, err := NewKeeper(cdc, invalidAddress, storeService, transientKey, ss)

}


## Tools Used
Remix IDE

func NewKeeper(

    authority sdk.AccAddress,
    storeService corestoretypes.KVStoreService,
    transientKey storetypes.StoreKey,
    ss paramstypes.Subspace,
) (Keeper, error) {
    // ensure authority account is correctly formatted
    if err := sdk.VerifyAddressFormat(authority); err != nil {
        return Keeper{}, err
    }

    return Keeper{
        cdc:          cdc,
        storeService: storeService,
        authority:    authority,
        transientKey: transientKey,
        ss:           ss,
    }, nil
}

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-canto/blob/main/canto-main/app/app.go#L823
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-canto/blob/main/ethermint-main/app/app.go#L695


# Vulnerability details

## Description
According to the [upgrading guide](https://github.com/cosmos/cosmos-sdk/blob/v0.50.6/UPGRADING.md) of cosmos sdk for version 0.50.6, when using (legacy) application wiring, the following must be added to app.go:

````Solidity
+app.ModuleManager.SetOrderPreBlockers(
+	upgradetypes.ModuleName,
+)

app.ModuleManager.SetOrderBeginBlockers(
-	upgradetypes.ModuleName,
)

````

However, in the app.go of Canto and Ethermint, the upgradetypes.ModuleName under SetOrderBeginBlockers has not been removed.

````Solidity
Canto App
File: app.go
823: 		upgradetypes.ModuleName, //@audit should be removed? 

Ethermint App
File: app.go
668: 		upgradetypes.ModuleName,//@audit should be removed
````

## Impact
Running the same module twice in a single block cycle can introduce unnecessary computational overhead. This redundancy can slow down block processing without adding any benefit.

## Proof of Concept
Consider this scenario, in every block processing, upgradetypes.ModuleName  will be executed twice, one in preblock phase and one in beginblock phase. This will delay the overall performance of Canto blockchain as well as unnecessary consumption of resources. 

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Remove the upgradetypes.ModuleName under SetOrderBeginBlockers as per upgrade guide.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-canto/blob/d1d51b2293d4689f467b8b1c82bba84f8f7ea008/ethermint-main/x/evm/types/msg.go#L78

## Impact

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-canto/blob/d1d51b2293d4689f467b8b1c82bba84f8f7ea008/ethermint-main/x/evm/types/msg.go#L78-L154

The newMsgEthereumTx function, which creates a new Ethereum transaction, does not handle the case where the chainID, gasPrice, or amount parameters are nil.

The issue occurs in the following code snippet:

`if chainID != nil {
    chainIDInt := sdkmath.NewIntFromBigInt(chainID)
    cid = &chainIDInt
}

if gasPrice != nil {
    gasPriceInt := sdkmath.NewIntFromBigInt(gasPrice)
    gp = &gasPriceInt
}

if amount != nil {
    amountInt := sdkmath.NewIntFromBigInt(amount)
    amt = &amountInt
}
`

If any of these parameters (chainID, gasPrice, or amount) are nil, the corresponding pointers (cid, gp, or amt) will not be assigned any value. And the code will proceed to other lines without reverting.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
When chainID, gasPrice, or amount are nil, the return value should be handled appropriately.

Context

## Proof of Concept

According to

https://github.com/cosmos/cosmos-sdk/blob/v0.50.6/UPGRADING.md#modules

> The following modules' Keeper methods now take in a context.Context instead of sdk.Context. Any module that has an interfaces for them (like "expected keepers") will need to update and re-generate mocks if needed:

x/authz
x/bank
x/mint
x/crisis
x/distribution
x/evidence
x/gov
x/slashing
x/upgrade

but many module such as coinswap, x/csr, x/epoch/keepers and x/govshuttle/ (which import x/gov) keeper still use sdk.Context instead of context.Context,

which result in incorrect interface mistmatch, some example code:

```solidity
// GetAuthority returns the x/govshuttle module's authority.
func (k Keeper) GetAuthority() string {
	return k.authority
}

func (k Keeper) Logger(ctx sdk.Context) log.Logger {
	return ctx.Logger().With("module", fmt.Sprintf("x/%s", types.ModuleName))
}

// retrieve the port address from state
func (k Keeper) GetPort(ctx sdk.Context) (common.Address, bool) {
	store := runtime.KVStoreAdapter(k.storeService.OpenKVStore(ctx))
	prefixStore := prefix.NewStore(store, types.PortKey)
	bz := prefixStore.Get(types.PortKey)
	// if not found return false
	if len(bz) == 0 {
		return common.Address{}, false
	}
	return common.BytesToAddress(bz), true
}
```
